popCulture.title: Philoctetes (mythology)
popCulture.description: Poeas' son inherits Heracles' bow — whether Poeas or Philoctetes lit the Oeta pyre, the father is the stem of the archer who takes Troy.

popCulture.title: Heracles
popCulture.description: Apollodorus makes Poeas the passer-by who lights Heracles' funeral pyre on Mount Oeta and receives the hero's bow and arrows in return.

popCulture.title: Poeas
popCulture.description: King of Meliboea (or Malis), Argonaut archer, father of Philoctetes — friend of Heracles at the pyre that ends the labours.

popCulture.title: Philoctetes
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' tragedy assumes the bow Poeas' house received from Heracles — the weapon the Greeks must reclaim from Lemnos.
